reason: The append-only session log, its envelope, the surface fold, derived history, fork seeds and crash closers are kept in Go form as the packages session, session/event, session/surface and session/core. Storage is called directly through the contract owned by area A05 instead of being a listener, and the live session holds folds instead of the whole event list.

Scoped registration is kept as the leaf package session/scope: an opaque key from a table, a tagged registration context on its own cordis fiber, layered registries with nearest-wins shadowing and scope-filtered dispatch. The single parent becomes an ordered list of enclosing scopes and the scope fiber no longer inherits its creator's services.
The deprecated synchronous reader eventAt has no Go counterpart: the live session does not hold the event list, and an old event is read through the paged, cancellable Read that may go to storage.

The deprecated synchronous reader snapshotEvents has no Go counterpart: there is no resident log to snapshot, ranges are read in pages, and fork reads its prefix from storage instead of from a snapshot of a live session.
The deprecated synchronous reader ownEvents has no Go counterpart: the header stores the inherited count, and the events a session owns are read in pages starting at that offset.

The silent trap is removed: a scope's context reaches no service, so calling a service through it fails with ErrNotInjected; a scoped event cannot be dispatched without a key; every service that accepts registrations declares Layered or Shared, and mounting a component that writes to a Shared one under a scope is reported. A Shared service stays shared, as its declared and catalogued contract.

Scope contexts cannot nest because every scope fiber hangs under the scope component, so hierarchy has one representation: the key's ordered list of enclosing scopes. That list may name several unrelated scopes, which gives the multi-membership upstream lacks, with the creator's order deciding shadowing.

The scope fiber's parent is a component that injects nothing, so a holder of the scope context reaches only the services its own component declares, never the creator's. Third-party code runs in plugin processes and never holds a context.

Fork names its source by id and reads the prefix from storage, so the source need not be live. A step cannot be closed while one of its tool calls has no result, so a Go log contains no closed step with a missing result for fork to repair.

There is no log-wide format version and no migration chain: each event type carries its own payload version with converters applied on read, the store reads only its own layout, and upstream files go through the separate deferred importer.

The turn/end payload has the reason kinds refusal and budget (the Go name for ACP's max_turn_requests) from payload version 1, and an unknown kind read from a newer log is preserved, so a producer needs no vocabulary or format change. Area A02's turn budget emits budget; refusal still needs a producer in areas A04 and A02, listed as an open question.

A fork records its source session and cut position in its own header fields, separate from a subagent's creator, so the tree of branches is a query over headers. Building the view belongs to area A06; the data that makes it possible is recorded here.
Replaced by the typed scoped event session.Created in the ordered dispatch form: the first listener error stops the dispatch and vetoes publication, as a synchronous throw does upstream.
Replaced by the typed scoped event session.Closed in the notify form, sent after the deliverer has delivered every event and carrying the id, header, final length and cause as values.

Replaced by the typed scoped event session.Committed in the notify form. One deliverer goroutine per session reads forward from a cursor and notifies in commit order outside the append lock, so a listener cannot fail or block an append.
No Go event: storage is no longer a set of listeners, so the durability barrier is the method Session.Flush, which calls the session's storage writer directly and returns the new durable offset.
ctx.sessions becomes the service key session.Key with the interface session.Service (Prepare, Create, Open, OpenRead, Fork, Get, Live), provided by the component core.Component.

The always-on guarantee that no reader can rewrite history is kept, but Go cannot deep-freeze. The committed payload is encoded once and held as an immutable Go string; readers decode their own copy, and no exported function returns memory the session still uses.

Kept: the session is an append-only log, the only source of truth, and model history is derived from it. Appends still do not wait for a disk sync; the Go session additionally holds folds instead of the event list.
Kept in full: an ordered surface maintained by append and replace operations with cited sources, validated by a plan before commit and applied after, as pure functions in session/surface.

The ignorable marker and the plugin: namespace are kept. The lint rule that limits the writer to experimental packages is replaced: plugin processes write records under their own owner segment by capability, and compiled-in experimental components declare ignorable types instead.

Kept: one settlement event per model attempt and no per-chunk events. The raw timed stream becomes the cold part of the payload so history reads stay small, and token usage stays in the hot part so no fold needs the stream.

Kept: the system prompt is an ordinary surface event at node 0, changed with the same append and replace operations, and the fold protects the head from any replacement that is not a system message over exactly that node.

Kept from the first Go version: one spelling per fact, required placement on surface events and none on log-only events. A typed envelope makes most alternative spellings unrepresentable and the remaining rules are checked at append and at open.

Adopted fully instead of as a deprecation: the Go session interface never offers synchronous access to arbitrary history, state after resume comes from checkpointed folds, and old events are read in pages.

Purity and ownership by the event's owner are kept, but registration as an unloadable effect is replaced: the rewrite function is declared statically with its event type and payload version, so it cannot be missing, needs no hand-over to offline readers, and old logs keep deriving the same history.
The Go format stores a tool result as its own tool-role message from the first version and keeps the closed set of five surface types; the upstream conversion from the wrapper form has no subject.
Adopted as the starting shape without the five migration stages: consumers use Session and Service, and storage is a provider interface that the session calls directly and that area A05 implements.

Adopted: a small logical core plus separate capabilities becomes three Go interfaces with one owner each: the session contract here, Storage for area A05 and the Folder hook for area A06, which also owns queries.

The upstream rejection is reversed, because Go has no declaration merging and a registry is the only way to extend the vocabulary. Upstream's objection that reads would depend on composition is met by declaring every compiled-in type statically and sealing the registry at boot.
Kept: a change to the visible tool set is a developer/message surface event whose additions are bound by headerSeq to an earlier request/header, checked when the append is planned.

The fingerprint policy exists for TypeScript union types. In Go the raw payload string is authoritative and decoding from the log tolerates unknown fields and kinds, so a new attribution kind is additive without a policy. Request-only input can enter a request only through a logged event that declares a builder.

Kept: request headers record the active tools and the session keeps a capability-independent tool-history fold that resolves additions through their historical header. Projecting it for each provider route belongs to area A04.

The rule that copied history is not delegation is kept: Creator and Origin are set only for subagents. The choice to record no source is changed: a fork records ForkSource and ForkThrough in separate fields, which avoids the misclassification that made upstream drop the link and makes a branch tree possible. No behaviour may depend on those fields.
Kept: a turn means one model-loop execution, log-only events may be appended between turns, and durability is an explicit Flush. The bracket check constrains only turn, step and tool-call events.
The rejection is kept: step/start and step/end stay in the core vocabulary, because step/end is the durable sign that a model request finished and both the closers and the bracket check depend on it.

title: The log is the only state, and a live session holds folds, not events
Three roles: the session contract, a storage provider, a fold hook
Immutability by encoding: the committed payload is an immutable string
The event vocabulary is declared statically and sealed at boot
One envelope, a payload version per type, hot and cold parts
A message rewrite is a pure function bound to an event type and payload version
Only the session can construct a model request, and a settlement records what it answered
The log refuses an unbalanced bracket, and closers are a function of fold state
Three live events; delivery is a tailing reader; flush is a method
A scope is a fiber for lifetime and a key for visibility, with no inherited service reach
Fork reads from storage, at any existing event, and records its origin apart from the creator
A log-only change reaches a session wherever it is held
A typed, versioned event vocabulary that every reader interprets the same way
A live session that accepts events in order, delivers them once and holds no history
Model history, the request header and the tool history are computed from the log
A model request can only come from the log and can be rebuilt from it
Brackets always balance: checked on append, closed on failure, crash and fork
Features can change what the model is shown through pure, versioned message rewrites
Any stored session can be forked at any event, with its lineage recorded
Per-agent and per-preset registrations with one owner and no borrowed authority
A log-only change can be recorded on a session this process does not drive
Declared types round-trip, old versions convert, unknown required types refuse and unknown ignorable ones survive unchanged
Every invalid envelope is refused with no change to length, history or feed
Concurrent appends get dense sequence numbers and are delivered once, in order
A group append is all or nothing in memory and in storage
No caller can change committed history through anything the session returned
A failing or slow feed listener cannot fail or delay an append, and delivery respects scope
Creation veto, ordered close, append after close and lease loss behave as specified
Reads are paged and include the unflushed tail, and session memory does not grow with the log
The incremental surface fold equals a fold from storage, and the planner never panics or half-applies
Derived history matches golden files and a snapshot never changes after it is taken
The request-header and tool-history folds follow the logged snapshots and historical header references
Every recorded request is rebuilt from its log prefix with the stored digest, and a request cannot be constructed outside the session
Closers are exact at every interruption point, and an unbalanced bracket is refused
Core fold checkpoint plus suffix replay equals full replay
Message rewrites are deterministic, identity-preserving, atomic and bound to their payload version
Fork of a live or stored session at any event yields an independent child with correct cut, closers and lineage
Scoped registrations are visible only in their scope and enclosed scopes and are gone after close
A scope context reaches no service, and a Shared registry under a scope is reported
A store that breaks a contract clause makes the session close with a classified error instead of folding bad data
A log-only change is appended live, by a maintenance append on a free session, or filed as a request, and is applied at most once
Requests received by a real model API equal requests rebuilt from the log
A host killed during a tool call resumes into a history a real provider accepts
